items.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022
items.q: the guy Bobby Mojica was great — he would come over to our house.

ctx.x: Well as a kid just his sound and the melodicism and the passion and the beautiful sound he got out of the trumpet. It was heartfelt. It made me cry. It made my dad cry when we’d hear him play a ballad. I remember, and I was only — he died when I was ten years old so this was early on I grew up with him, at least the last five or six years of his career when he was in Philly dad had all the records. He’d play a ballad and I remember Dad kind of grabbed me and said, “Randy, trumpet’s the greatest jazz instrument.”…

Collins, and there were some really good players, and the guy Bobby Mojica was great — he would come over to our house. So I think he was like a friend even though we never met him. I had never heard him play. Dad would go hear him all the time. I wish I could have. I knew his wife very well. After he passed away she was around on the scene quite a bit. But what a sound. I don’t think — there are certain things he did that have never been surpassed, just the melodicism, the beauty of everything he played.
Yeah. The “Clifford Brown with Strings” — when he enters in that first cut it’s like whoa.
